name: Task_9
description:
Generate finite-temperature molecular dynamics trajectories of bulk Copper and train a Ridge regression model on Smooth Overlap of Atomic Positions (SOAP) descriptors to predict instantaneous potential energies. Start with a conventional face-centered cubic (FCC) unit cell of Copper (a = 3.615 \u00c5) expanded into a 2 \u00d7 2 \u00d7 2 supercell. Use the MACE-MP-0 foundation model as the calculator. Conduct molecular dynamics simulations in the canonical (NVT) ensemble at 800 K, choosing and justifying the integration, thermostat, equilibration, production, and sampling settings. Retain 200 chronological production configurations with instantaneous total potential energies from the main 800 K trajectory. Compute one global SOAP descriptor per configuration using the dscribe library, choosing and justifying the descriptor settings, preprocessing, and Ridge regularization. Compare randomized-split and time-aware validation on the main trajectory using the same training and evaluation counts, protecting both holdouts from model selection and fitting preprocessing only on each training partition. Save a final structure-to-prediction pipeline trained on the main trajectory and freeze it before evaluating the independent trajectories; submit the JSON answer specified below.

Use the supplied 32-atom cell and generate three additional independent trajectories at 800, 500, and 1100 K with distinct recorded velocity seeds and 200 production frames each, for 800 labeled structures in total. Start each run from the supplied cell, remove center-of-mass momentum, and preserve the fixed cell, atoms, and velocities from equilibration into production. Assess equilibration for all four runs. The evaluator derives MAE/RMSE/R² for both validation strategies and all independent tests from the submitted energy labels and predictions, and includes the main energy series' correlation time or supported bound when available. Assess production temperatures and sampling limitations in your analysis; those diagnostics are not required submission fields. Inspect temporal dependence and temperature transfer without assuming a metric ordering. Retain the trajectory and regression calculations with your own code.

Use a timestep of at most 2 fs and retain at least 16 equilibration samples per run. Production duration is flexible; a resolved correlation estimate requires at least 10 correlation times of production and consistency across trajectory windows; supported bounds are accepted.
